title: Assessing the Vulnerability and the Stock Status of the Bluntnose Sixgill Shark, Hexanchus griseus, in North‐Eastern Tunisia (Central Mediterranean) Using Data‐Limited Models
content:
ABSTRACT

The bluntnose sixgill shark (Hexanchus griseus) is classified as ‘Near Threatened’ at a global level but currently holds a ‘Least Concern’ status in the Mediterranean Sea, despite increasing fishing pressure and insufficient data. This study presents the first comprehensive stock assessment of H. griseus in north-eastern Tunisia (GFCM GSA 13), which challenges the regional assessment. We analysed a 22-year catch time series (2003–2024) and length-frequency data from 192 specimens, using two data-limited models: length-based Bayesian biomass (LBB) and catch-maximum sustainable yield (CMSY++). Our results reveal a population dominated by juveniles and subadults (120–393 cm) in the sampled catches, with no individuals reaching the reported size at maturity (441 cm). The catch data show a significant downward trend since 2003 (p < 0.05), with a breakpoint in 2015 indicating lower production (p < 0.01). The LBB model indicates extreme H. griseus biomass depletion (B/B 0 = 0.17; B/B MSY = 0.48) and that fishing mortality exceeds natural mortality (F/M = 1.7). The CMSY++ model shows a low intrinsic growth rate (r = 0.078 year−1) and a terminal biomass of 78% of the maximum sustainable yield. These findings challenge the species' regional status, as they demonstrate unsustainable exploitation. We recommend the following immediate management measures: implementing a minimum conservation reference size (MCRS, Lc opt) of 287 cm, investigating and potentially protecting areas that may serve as juvenile habitats and enhancing monitoring. This study highlights the importance of using data-limited models to inform conservation efforts and emphasises the need to reassess H. griseus conservation status in the region.
